pairs_rule: the verdict pair is judged by the totals block with the hard and guard metrics below; the two reported pairs are judged by the same rule and their verdicts go in N06.9's note (N06's decisions: one switch per bug; a failing batch is bisected switch by switch, and these pairs are that bisection, run up front as N06.9 asks)

boards.eligibility: every row; no row is dropped after a number. Chosen before any number: canary-pwr through the plugin's DSN and argument list (N06's 'canary-pwr through the plugin path'), K09's three stripped demos, and the two DAC2020 fixtures that Java's PORT_LEDGER reports fully routed or optimized (bm01 'fully routed, 5 optimizer passes', bm02), because the optimizer's preflight guard 1 skips the stage on a board with an unrouted connection

canary-plugin45.grade: canary grade.sh steps against canary-pwr-rev1.0 at canary b1994423 (N05.3's canary-plugin45 grading)
canary-plugin45.why: Dan's plugin run (N05.3's row). The plugin path leaves connections unrouted on this board, so guard 1 is expected to skip the optimizer in every arm; optimizer_bypassed says whether it did, and then the four sessions must be byte-identical

bm01.grade: freerouting-dev gate collect's statistics of the imported SES (no KiCad board): unrouted, clearance_violations, vias, length_mm, via_in_pad; below_minimum from freerouting-dev widths; drc_real not graded

interf_u.grade: tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh <input> -- <arm command> (strips tracks and vias, exports the DSN, routes, grades with kicad-cli), plus tools/kicad-oracle/via_in_pad.py on the routed board

boards.procedure: demos: tracks and vias stripped by tools/kicad-oracle/kicad_steps.py strip (K09.json's boards; the hashes below are of the stripped boards)

grading: WSL KiCad 10.0.7 for the demo and canary rows, one job at a time; the DSN rows by Freerouting's board model. When two arms' sessions are byte-identical the session is graded once, the earlier arm's grade (order java, first_pass, equal_key, both). The canary sessions go to target/canary-handoff/ for canary's official grade

metric_definitions.via_in_pad: demos and canary: tools/kicad-oracle/via_in_pad.py on the routed board (session vias only); DSN rows: freerouting-dev gate collect's count on the imported SES
metric_definitions.below_minimum: demos and canary: KiCad track_width errors; DSN rows: the nets with copper under their class width in freerouting-dev widths <DSN> <SES> (under_mm > 0), the board model's version of the same limit
metric_definitions.clearance_violations: the router's clearance violations of the final board (result.json board_statistics; gate collect's clearance_violations)
metric_definitions.drc_real: KiCad error-severity items other than unconnected items and starved thermals, minus the same types on the unrouted input; DSN rows: not graded
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: KiCad's unconnected items after importing the session; DSN rows fall back to unrouted (the totals signal)
metric_definitions.unrouted: the router's final unrouted count (result.json board_statistics connections.incomplete_count)
metric_definitions.length_mm: the session's total trace length (gate collect's length_mm)
metric_definitions.optimizer_score: result.json's optimizer_score of the final board
metric_definitions.optimizer_bypassed: 1 if the job log has 'Skipping optimization stage' (a preflight guard skipped the optimizer), else 0
metric_definitions.optimizer_passes: result.json phases.optimizer.passes_completed (0 when bypassed); opt_first_pass_stops=false adds at most one pass where a pass cleared the increased ripup costs inside itself
metric_definitions.wall_seconds: the CLI process's wall time; time is reported, not judged (D2: routing is deterministic, wall time is not); N06.9 asks that the registration records it because opt_first_pass_stops adds a pass

keep_rule: N06's accept rule for (b) fixes: a batch is accepted when the hard guards hold, no board regresses by more than twice its noise band and the total is not worse than the set's noise; a neutral fix stays in. If the verdict pair passes, N06.13 turns both keys off in ENHANCED through N05; if it fails, the reported pairs say which switch to keep, and a switch whose own pair passes may still be accepted alone
stop_rule: one registered run per arm per row; no reruns with other settings
not_registered: the A14 exact set: legacy keeps both keys true, so A14 is unaffected; N06.3's A14 run covers the defaults
canary-pwr through canary's graded CLI flow (Q10's 33): the plugin row stands for canary-pwr, as N06 asks
a run with the optimizer's preflight guards off (they decide whether the optimizer runs at all; not a batch-O question)
seen_before_registration: only the unit and fixture tests of N06.9: on bm08 with its routed session unfixed and no autoroute pass per candidate (every candidate fails), opt_first_pass_stops=true runs 1 optimizer pass and false runs 2 (tests/batch_optimizer.rs first_pass_switch_both_behaviours); opt_equal_key_skip=false adds the two items given an equal key by equal_key_switch_keeps_every_candidate. No routed number of any registered row, under any arm

decision_table.pass: N06.9's measurement [x]; N06.13 turns opt_first_pass_stops and opt_equal_key_skip off in ENHANCED (N05) with their DIVERGENCES 'Profile enhanced' lines
decision_table.fail: the failing switch stays true in both profiles, with these numbers in N06.9 and N06.13; the other switch is judged by its own reported pair

N06.9's diff has been on main since its registration; the two keys still default to true in both profiles and are not in ENHANCED. The registered engine text was: "freerouting-rs at origin/main 7a4f73b with N06.9's diff, one Linux release build for every arm; the default profile (enhanced, whose ENHANCED table does not touch java_quirks), the optimizer on (the default), so the arms differ only in the two router.java_quirks keys". (2) Profile: Profile enhanced at ed603f5 is not the enhanced of the registration: N06.13 (main e0610fc, confirmed by ed603f5's note) put 30 router.java_quirks keys to false in ENHANCED (crates/freerouting/src/settings/profile.rs): any_angle_skip_length_squared, connect_to_trace_swapped_width, drc_units_10000_per_mm, drill_destination_room_index, dsn_class_class_pairs, dsn_shape_bbox, dsn_unit_ignored, dsn_via_alias, edge_corner_not_advanced, failed_attempt_ripped_carryover, fanout_pin_order_names, fanout_stale_drill_carry, in_front_of_pad_side0_flank, in_front_of_pad_typo, init_failure_room_leak, move_drill_tidy_region, ortho_zero_width_room, pull_tight_reused_lines_change, rational_perp_projection, route_change_layer_no_via, route_connect_inner_break, route_result_int_via_ratio, rules_matrix_trees_not_rebuilt, rules_unknown_layer_scope, select_extension_ignores_filter, ses_reader_scale, smooth_loses_trace, snapshot_drops_compensation, stats_line_ab_length, store_trace_class_self_compare. Every arm therefore gives --router.profile explicitly, and an arm under enhanced means enhanced with those 30 fixes, besides N05's stages. Each arm's command now names the binary and gives --router.profile=enhanced right after --gui.enabled=false (the registered java command was "freerouting -de {DSN} -do {SES} --gui.enabled=false --result-json {OUT}/result.json {ROW_FLAGS}"); the arms' settings are unchanged (enhanced is the default), so the arms still differ only in the two keys. (3) Memory: no row routes in any-angle mode (canary-pwr's plugin DSN, bm01, bm02 and the three KiCad demos are 45-degree boards), so N06.16's router.java_quirks.any_angle_room_side_index keeps its default (true) in every arm, the same value everywhere; every route runs under an 8000000 kB address-space cap (ulimit -v), one route, one kicad-cli and one KiCad Python at a time; the cap changes no routing work. (4) Runner: tools/bench/n06_run.py cannot run this registration (per-row ROW_FLAGS, {OUT}, the demo rows through grade.sh), so a run script substitutes {DSN}, {SES}, {OUT} and {ROW_FLAGS} into each arm's command as registered: the canary-plugin45, bm01 and bm02 rows run the command directly; each demo row runs tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh --out <arm dir> <demo .kicad_pcb> -- <the command, under the cap>, then tools/kicad-oracle/via_in_pad.py on the routed board. Every route appends --stats json --stats-out {OUT}/stats.json to its arm's command (statistics only observe; the same flags in every arm), because result.json's phases.optimizer.duration_seconds is null at ed603f5: optimizer_seconds is the sum of the stats' optimizer_pass stage seconds, and wall_seconds the runner's wall time of the CLI process. The canary-plugin45 session is graded as registered with canary's grade.sh steps against canary-pwr-rev1.0 at canary b1994423: canary hardware/tools at 2a7e070b (git archive; the first revision whose grade.sh takes GRADE_REV, the tools every N06 run used) with GRADE_REV=b1994423, ses_import.py, DRC with schematic parity and refilled zones, via_in_pad.py and inner_tracks.py, on WSL KiCad 10.0.7. Each distinct canary-plugin45 session is graded twice on separate copies and the first grade counts (KiCad's grade of identical bytes has moved a clearance count, N06.12's note); the second is reported. The grading text's 'byte-identical sessions share the earlier arm's grade' is unchanged. (5) Hard metrics on every row, so that none is null for freerouting-dev gate --prereg: via_in_pad and below_minimum are option (b), no new breach versus baseline: the arm's count minus the java arm's on the same row, floored at 0, with the raw counts reported as via_in_pad_raw and below_minimum_raw. Raw counts: demos via_in_pad.py's vias_in_pads and KiCad track_width errors; canary-plugin45 canary's via_in_pad.py count and KiCad track_width errors; bm01 and bm02 one measuring tool on the engine at ed603f5 for every arm (N06.4 amendment 2's and N06.8 amendment 1's: the input's session wiring stripped before the SES is imported, the SES read at the writer's scale): vias in an SMD pad the input has no via for, and below_minimum as registered, the nets with copper under their class width (the tool's below_class_width_nets; its count of traces under the narrowest class width is reported). drc_real on the demo rows is grade.sh's drc_real minus its starved_thermal count (the registered definition excludes starved thermals; grade.sh already subtracts the input's types and excludes unconnected items), on canary-plugin45 KiCad's error-severity items other than unconnected items and starved thermals plus schematic parity items; DSN rows not graded (null, a guard). clearance_violations on every row is the router's (result.json board_statistics). (6) Verdict: freerouting-dev gate --prereg (built at ed603f5) with --all-pairs (the verdict pair java/both and the two reported single-switch pairs) on records built from the runs; each record row's board is the row's registered board name (canary-plugin45's is canary-pwr), so the registered noise bands apply; bm01 and bm02 take the default band from their connections. optimizer_bypassed reads the job log's 'Skipping optimization stage'. Neither switch has a run_stats counter: reach is read from optimizer_passes and the sessions. The rows, metrics, rule, noise bands, keep rule and decision table are unchanged. (7) seen_before_registration is unchanged; since registration and before this amendment: earlier checklists routed canary-plugin45 (N05.3, Q14) and the three demos (K09 and the Q series) under other engines and settings, and Java's PORT_LEDGER reports bm01 and bm02; no routed number of any row under this engine, profile and arms was seen
